decisions.reason: Both CPs discuss compliance investment and programs, but CH04 is a general rule/conclusion while CH05 lists specific measures. Neither provides a concrete framework that the other directly expands or applies; they are related topics at different levels of detail.

CH03 provides an explicit comparison framework between terrorism financing and money laundering (goals, sources, pathways). CH02 discusses their connection and shared techniques. Reviewing the CH03 comparison directly helps distinguish the concepts mentioned in CH02.

CH04 provides the concrete definitions and classification of regulated vs. obliged entities, along with their specific obligations. CH05 directly applies and specializes this by identifying which specific institutions fall into the obliged entity category and why they are high-risk.

CH01 introduces the three-stage money laundering framework (placement, layering, integration). CH03 directly expands and applies this exact framework in its detailed discussion of the money laundering process.

CH01 defines financial crime and lists its types (ML, fraud, etc.). CH05 classifies financial crime risks (operational, legal, systemic, etc.). These are different classification schemes; CH05 does not directly apply or expand CH01's definition/types framework.
